basis: Team recommendation adopted on the leader's instruction. Base 20 years: the Revenue Department tax depreciation rate for durable buildings is 5 percent of cost a year (input row asset_useful_life_by_type_nesdc_years), which corresponds to 20 years for the building component. That is a tax rate, not an economic life. Low 20 is the lower bound of the ADB (2017) horizon of 20 to 30 years (input rows adb_economic_horizon_years_low and _high). High 25 is the upper bound of the ADB operating life for dams and railways of 20 to 25 years (input rows adb_dam_railway_operating_years_low and _high).
status: assumption (team recommendation adopted; anchored to sourced ranges; not sourced as a Thai value)

basis: Base and high use the ADB (2017) illustrative implementation period of 2 years (input row adb_illustrative_implementation_years). The low case adds one year for a complex of this size. That step is a judgement and is not sourced.

Team recommendation adopted on the leader's instruction. Base 0.08 is the NESDC (2024) social discount rate of 7 percent plus one point for operator risk. No financial rate for a Thai theme park was found in the sources, so this is an assumption. Low 0.10 is two points above the base for a more pessimistic operator. High 0.07 equals the NESDC social rate. The ADB (2017) standard EIRR of 0.09 (input row discount_rate_eirr_standard) is an economic hurdle and is not used. The Thai 10-year government bond yield of 2.32 percent (input row thailand_10y_government_bond_yield_2026_10_14) is a floor reference and is not a WACC.

Team recommendation adopted: the working value is kept. The base is the Hong Kong Disneyland FY2025 attendance reported by the operator (input row hk_disneyland_attendance_fy2025). Base is Hong Kong Disneyland attendance in fiscal 2025 (input row hk_disneyland_attendance_fy2025). Low is Ocean Park attendance in fiscal 2024/25 (input row ocean_park_attendance_fy2024_25). High is Shanghai Disneyland attendance in 2024 (input row shanghai_disneyland_attendance_2024_million), which is a TEA estimate. These parks are comparables and not the Thai complex. The demand study has not reported.
status: generalized (Hong Kong Disneyland FY2025 base; Ocean Park FY2024/25 low; Shanghai Disneyland 2024 high)

basis: Base is the share of Hong Kong Disneyland visitors who are not local residents in fiscal 2019, 59 percent, which is 100 minus the 41 percent local share (input row hk_disneyland_visitor_share_local_fy2019; a copy on a secondary blog, not confirmed). Low 0.36 is an assumed value. It was once taken as the Ocean Park non-local share in fiscal 2024/25 (1.25 of 3.46 million), but that count is not confirmed (input row ocean_park_non_local_visitors_fy2024_25 is pending). High is not anchored and is an assumed 75 percent. The non-local count includes mainland visitors, which the model treats as international visitors.
status: generalized (Hong Kong Disneyland FY2019 base, itself unconfirmed; low is an assumed value after an unconfirmed Ocean Park anchor; high not anchored)

basis: Team recommendation adopted: the working value is kept. No source exists; the labelled range is the sensitivity. No comparable value in the project sources. Share of international visits that are new to Thailand or to its tourism spending. Placeholder for the segment study.

Team recommendation adopted: the working value is kept. No source exists; the labelled range is the sensitivity. Share of gross spending moved from other Thai destinations or activities. The low case is the highest displacement. No source in the project sources. Placeholder for the segment study.

Team decisions adopted for the base and high cases: the labelled placeholders of 10,000 and 20,000 THB are kept. The low case is the sourced on-site benchmark: Oriental Land's Tokyo Disney Resort per-guest merchandise (5,227 yen) and food and beverage (3,569 yen) sales for FY3/2026, 8,796 yen in total, converted at about 0.205 THB per yen (an indicative third-party rate of mid-2026; the Bank of Thailand rate is to replace it). The benchmark measures on-site spending only, so it is a floor for incremental visitors and not a base. The per-trip figures (TAT 2023 at 50,900 THB; MoTS 2019 at 48,580 THB) are per trip, not per park visit, and are not used. Values are labelled assumptions for the spending study.
status: assumption (labelled grid; low case from a sourced on-site benchmark, pending the Bank of Thailand rate)

basis: Team recommendation adopted: the working value is kept. No source exists; the labelled range is the sensitivity. Share of net spending that stays in the Thai economy after imports and leakage. Placeholder for the economic study.

The tax base is not documented, so this is a placeholder. Base is 7 divided by 107, the tax-inclusive share of spending at the reduced 7 percent VAT rate in force from 1 October 2026 (input row vat_reduced_rate_2026_2027). High is 10 divided by 110, at the statutory 10 percent rate (input row vat_statutory_rate). Low captures no tax.

Base is Hong Kong Disneyland fiscal 2025 costs as a share of revenue: (8694 minus 536) divided by 8694, which is 0.9383. Low is Ocean Park fiscal 2024/25 costs as a share of revenue: (1280 plus 274.7) divided by 1280, which is 1.2146, using the press revenue of HK$1.28 billion. High is not anchored and is an assumed 0.70. Both anchors are total costs implied by net profit or loss. They include depreciation, financing and tax. Depreciation is included by the leader's decision, so the anchors are total costs as implied by net profit or loss and are not restated to cash operating cost. The overlap with the capital cost in the operator ledger, and in the national ledger, is kept, which makes the operating results pessimistic.
status: generalized (Hong Kong Disneyland FY2025 base; Ocean Park FY2024/25 low; high not anchored)

basis: Base is the Hong Kong Disneyland adult Tier 1 ticket of HK$669 (input row hk_disneyland_adult_ticket_tier1_hkd), converted at 4.3 baht per Hong Kong dollar. The rate is the Bank of Thailand reference rate of 33.52 baht per US dollar on 12 October 2026 (input row exchange_rate_thb_per_usd) divided by an assumed 7.8 Hong Kong dollars per US dollar. High is the Tier 4 peak adult ticket of HK$939 (input row hk_disneyland_adult_ticket_tier4_peak_hkd) at the same rate. Low is 25 percent below the base for discounts and resident or child pricing, a grid choice. Adult list prices are an upper reference for average revenue per visit.
status: generalized (Hong Kong Disneyland adult prices at an assumed exchange rate; low is a grid discount)

basis: Base 10.66 nights is an unsourced placeholder. No fetched source was located for it, and no input row backs it. High is an assumed 5 nights. Low is an assumed 12 nights. The accommodation cap is inversely proportional to this value.
No source in the project sources. Placeholder for the average number of guests in an occupied room.

Definition used by visits_from_passengers. A round trip through the same airport counts two passenger movements. A visit that uses two airports counts one movement at each. Base and low use the round trip. High uses the two-airport case.

Base is the budget year 2024 figure of 370,210 passengers at U-Tapao, 1 October 2023 to 30 September 2024, from the operator's air traffic chart (input row utapao_passengers_oct2023_sep2024). The chart does not say whether counts include arrivals plus departures. Low is an assumed higher load and high an assumed lower load. No calendar 2024 total is confirmed; the Ministry file sum of 384,881 has an inferred year and is not used.

No planned addition is sourced in the form the model needs. The 0 percent on the EEC Office page applies only to a private-sector subsection, so no overall progress figure is confirmed. A February 2026 news report gives 2031 as the target year for operations (input row utapao_expansion_opening_year), but it gives no capacity. Base and low are zero. High assumes a second terminal with the same capacity as the current 3.7 million passengers (input row utapao_terminal_capacity_passengers_per_year). The EEC project target of 60 million passengers per year is undated and is not used.

No source in the project sources. Placeholder for the public operating cost borne by the government after construction, such as upkeep of access roads and utilities. The primary fiscal ledger also charges the complex capital cost to the government in the construction years, using the proposal value, which is not verified. The variant without that capital cost is reported alongside.

Pattaya city hotel keys from CBRE (input row pattaya_hotel_keys_h2_2024, H2 2024), used as a proxy for the room stock that serves the complex. The complex site is not stated as Pattaya, and no Chon Buri room count is found (input row chonburi_accommodation_rooms_2024_or_2025 is pending). The same value is used in all three cases.
status: generalized (Pattaya city hotel keys as proxy for the Chon Buri room stock)

basis: Average occupancy of Chon Buri in 2024 is 80.42 percent (National Statistical Office Table 17.1, input row chonburi_occupancy_2024_tat). This replaces the Pattaya CBRE figure of 71.0 percent used earlier. The room stock is still a Pattaya proxy, and the same value is used in all three cases. The occupancy ceiling is close to this value, so the free room stock is small; see occupancy_ceiling_serving_site.
status: generalized (official Chon Buri occupancy for 2024 combined with the Pattaya room stock, a proxy)

basis: Practical maximum average occupancy. The accommodation headroom is the free room stock up to this ceiling, rooms times (ceiling minus occupancy), floored at zero, so that headroom is not measured to 100 percent occupancy. The low case is the highest 2024 occupancy observed in any Thai province: Chon Buri at 80.42 percent (National Statistical Office Table 17.1, input row chonburi_occupancy_2024_tat). Chon Buri ranks first of the 77 rows of the table, including Bangkok, and the next value is 80.12 percent. Under the low case the market has no free rooms, so the low case has no accommodation headroom. The base case (85 percent) and high case (90 percent) are assumed practical maximums above any observed rate. No source gives a ceiling. A base ceiling anchored to the observed maximum (80.42 percent) would give zero headroom in the base case as well.
status: assumption (low anchored to the highest 2024 occupancy of any province; base and high assumed; not sourced)
